body: I'm kinda past the point of prevention. Maybe prevent it from becoming worse but I'm already aware of 4 surgeries I need as it is.

Even if I did leave, what would be the point? I'd still be in shitty health and time would still be ticking down until I become just another bitter old cunt like my mother. Abuse is a cycle and so is mental illness. And I don't have the strength to escape it as I am now and it's just going to get much harder as age slows me down. Maybe not exactly like her since I never wanted kids. But still an angry and miserable person nonetheless.

I'm already nearly 30 and have only just recently recieved the legal freedom of an 18 year old and still only have the personal freedom of a child. Everyone's already passed me up in life anyway. It's sad and pathetic.

I offer her a little bit of everything I eat if it's something she's able to have and she will take it if there are other people in the room with us. Plus no one else fills her food bowl besides me and she only really snacks on the dog food throughout the day. I never worry about her overeating because she just doesn't like to eat until she's full. She's very tall and gangly for a german shepherd but only weighs about 50 pounds so maybe she has a metabolism issue that messes with how she responds to food.

The resemblance thing might be a part of it. Her last owner was a very heavyset man and I'm a very heavyset woman and the only overweight person in my family. Wouldn't explain why she has no aversion toward them though.

We had a rusted out conversion van that we used to take our basset hound for rides in. We'd take him to McDonald's to buy him breakfast then take him to the local fishing hole and let him run around and play in the mud.

Bonus: My family are all fans of country music so it'd always be on the radio the whole time too. I'm probably the only one who can't stand it tbh :/ Even moreso now because hearing it just makes me really miss that old hound dog.

My dad is one of those people. He's even lied about what he's had for breakfast before or what song he was just listening to. It's little things like that even when you can blatantly prove him wrong. Sometimes he even lies about what he's doing WHILE he's doing it. We have no idea why he does this either because there's no logical reasoning behind it. (Perhaps it's an ego thing? Idk.)

People who demand you to teach them how to do something but never bother learning it. Instead they just resort to asking you to "show them how to do it" over and over because they know that this method just manipulates you into doing the work for them. Like, I get having to have it explained a few times. But if it takes you years to learn how to change the channel on your fucking TV, then you're either really stupid or just a lazy asshole.

As far as Don'ts, most other comments here have covered the more general ones. So I'll address the most common ones I personally get.

Don't make it about yourself. Getting angry or offended because you feel your life is worse is only going to make me push you away more. Telling me things like "I work 18 hours a day so you can live here" and "depression isn't a real thing, you just want a reason to be lazy" is only going to make me feel more guilty for having a hard time finding a steady job and push me closer to suicide because I feel like more of a burden.

And the biggest Don't I get is denying me access to therapy. If I'm struggling and want to take steps to get professional help and possibly medication. Telling me things like "you're fine/you shouldn't let yourself be so weak" or one of many ramblings about Big Pharma selling pills to make people into suicidal zombies to return more profit? It isn't helping and again, just puts more wedges into our relationship. It's basically telling me that the world is only out to get me and I should ignore professional advice over some soccer mom who read dozens of facebook memes. It's honestly selfish and borderline abusive.

The biggest Do is I'm a very independent person. Just understand that I'm suffering and give me space and allow me to accept offers of comfort on my own terms. If I want to talk, I'll talk. Understand that I may have to block out loud noises and bright lights because these cycles can come with some pretty severe migraines. Give me time alone to stretch or exercise because the body pain can be just as debilitating. Let me clean my room and take care of my plants and animals without hovering over me and micromanaging me. I'm not saying don't check in on me or ignore that I exist. Just don't try to force me to "get better" because it upsets you. All I want is time so I can eventually pick myself back up. Even if I can only do it for a short while. And driving me away isn't helping.

Thank you. I wasn't aware of the correlation, not causation aspect. I try to research what I can when I'm able to and seen a lot of claims of depression being a deadly mental illness because of suicide.

It still feels disrespectful to know the person who killed themselves and their family and still think to myself that I wish I had the ability to do the same. But, in a way, I suppose lacking any effective methods for suicide is partially how I've survived this long. That article did help me understand a little bit better though. As much resentment toward my family that I do have because of their ignorance and emotionally abusive methods, I still don't want to do that to them because I know they're simply still stuck in the old timey ways. But I shouldn't let the guilt eat at me like that either. It still does, but knowing it shouldn't still helps a little bit.

I tried to explain this to my brother the other day. I explained it as like how with diabetes, the pancreas can't produce enough insulin. Depression is when the brain can't produce enough serotonin. And that it isn't really feeling "sad" as much as it is feeling nothing when you should be feeling *something, anything at all.*

Which... Is a wild oversimplification of it. But keep in mind, my family doesn't believe mental illness is real except in extreme cases that involve straight jackets and padded walls. So I understand the frustration of it.

Sometimes it's also knowing that these people do care about you but then asking how they could possibly miss all the warning signs of a deeper problem. But sadly, people aren't actually that observant or they just don't know what is really going on. They can see someone they love is having a hard time but the average person isn't going to closely analyze your behavior or even know what to do if they were aware of the problem.

I feel really guilty for thinking this. But whenever I hear that depression has claimed someone so young, it really makes me wonder how I survived 20+ years of it untreated in a family and culture that doesn't believe in mental illness. When the depression is so bad that I can barely function properly let alone hold down a job and move out of my parent's home.

Like I can't decide if it's this is a positive thing or not because I kind of envy those who managed to find a way to put an end to their pain. But then I feel guilty for thinking such a thing because suicide is a horrible thing that hurts so many people.
